Nina Park: PulseMed goes live 08:00 PT tomorrow. they9re on a short pilot, high churn risk if latency is bad. need a short customer-facing "faststart" runbook covering tenant-prefill, streaming fallback, and renewal signals.
Carlos Mendes: got it. traffic estimate?
Nina Park: steady ~30 qps, burst to ~180 qps first 45m. PHI-sensitive no external caches.
Priya Singh: runbook bullets I recommend:
- tenant-prefill: top-40 query prefixes, run 4m before go-live, 2m TTL sliding refresh
- warm pool: scale to 3 pods (dedicated tenant) for first 90m, then scale down
- batching: 8ms window, disable if p95 >120ms
- streaming fallback when prefill miss exceeds 180ms
Theo Marsh: ops snippets:
curl -X POST https://console.api.redwood/prefill -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP" -d '{"tenant":"pulse","prefixes":["mrn:","note:","med:"]}'
POST /admin/prefill/dryrun {"tenant":"pulse","sample_size":150} -> returns hit estimate
Priya Singh: telemetry to cs-ops channel: p99_ms, prefill_hit_pct, active_warm_pods. set renewal_watch if hit_pct < 45 after 30m.
Nina Park: legal asks: mark cache entries tenant-only + kms-locked. add to runbook checklist.
Carlos Mendes: fallback plan: switch to quantized-mid model, batch-size=1, enable streaming-only; create incident if OOM.
deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: prefill-runner v1.9 at 1775011205
Nina Park: I'll draft the customer-facing one-pager and DM PulseMed. please review by EOD.
